deals.evidence: an option to purchase an expansion team for $25 million when he retired
deals.headline: Beckham's $25m expansion option becomes Inter Miami
deals.summary: Beckham's LA Galaxy contract gave him an option to buy an MLS expansion team for $25 million; he exercised it in 2014 and the league approved the Miami club, launched on 29 January 2018 (club history page). Forbes reports MLS once offered him $50 million to take the option back.

deals.evidence: The deal enables Jorge and Jose Mas and David Beckham to buyout the 48% of shares held by Marcelo Claure and Masayoshi Son in the club
deals.headline: Mas brothers and Beckham buy out Claure and Son
deals.investor: Jorge Mas, Jose Mas and David Beckham
deals.summary: The remaining owners bought the 48% held by Marcelo Claure and Masayoshi Son, financed alongside Ares' preferred equity; the sale reportedly valued the club in the region of $600 million (Sportico reported $600-650 million). The Raine Group advised the club.

deals.evidence: has closed a $150 million preferred equity deal with Inter Miami CF
deals.headline: Ares closes $150m preferred equity investment in Inter Miami
deals.summary: Funds managed by Ares' Credit Group took $150 million of preferred equity (which, Inside World Football notes, carries no control) as the Mas brothers and Beckham bought out Claure and Son. Sportico says Ares is believed to be the first private equity firm to invest in an MLS club.

deals.evidence: The City of Miami Commission made the people of Miami’s dream a reality, by voting to approve Miami Freedom Park.
deals.headline: Miami commission approves Miami Freedom Park
deals.investor: City of Miami (land lease to the owners' Miami Freedom Park venture)
deals.summary: The City of Miami Commission approved Miami Freedom Park on the city-owned Melreese site, a 99-year lease and development agreement (The Real Deal) for the stadium, hotel, offices, retail and a 58-acre public park, after voters approved it in a 2018 referendum on condition of private financing.

deals.evidence: has closed on a $75 million preferred equity stake in Inter Miami, marking its second investment into the MLS franchise
deals.headline: Ares adds $75m of preferred equity after Messi's arrival
deals.summary: Ares' second investment in the club, again preferred equity; the club said the money would fund growth initiatives including the stadium project. Structure and implied valuation were not disclosed.

deals.evidence: Billionaire Jorge Mas, David Beckham and Ares Management nabbed a $450 million loan for a planned soccer stadium in Miami that is already under construction.
deals.headline: JPMorgan lends $450m to build Miami Freedom Park stadium
deals.summary: The Mas-Beckham-Ares partnership developing the $1 billion Miami Freedom Park took a $450 million construction loan from JPMorgan Chase Bank, secured by the stadium and surrounding entertainment, concessions and retail space on the 58-acre site leased from the city.

deals.evidence: announced a stadium naming rights partnership with Brazilian digital financial services company Nu
deals.headline: Nu takes naming rights to Inter Miami's new stadium
deals.summary: Stadium naming rights partnership with the Brazilian digital bank; terms and length undisclosed, though Sportico was told it is one of the largest naming-rights deals for a soccer-specific stadium in MLS history.

stadium_owner.detail: Built and held by the owners' Miami Freedom Park joint venture (Mas brothers, Beckham, Ares) on city-owned land (the former Melreese golf course) leased from the City of Miami for 99 years; Forbes says the stadium was privately funded at an estimated $350 million. Opened 4 April 2026; the club previously played at Chase Stadium in Fort Lauderdale, owned by that city.

founded_evidence: JANUARY 29, 2018 Officially launched as Major League Soccer’s 25th Club
name: Club Internacional de Fútbol Miami
notes: Revenue, operating income (Forbes' EBITDA-style measure) and value are Forbes estimates for the 2025 season (list of 13 Feb 2026, cited via the Wayback Machine copy because forbes.com refuses scripted fetches; Forbes' May 2026 world list repeats $1.35bn, $200m and $50m). The revenue breakdown is Sportico's rough 2024 estimate (about $90m each from matchday and commercial, out of $190m). Other figures: Sportico put local revenue at $215m in 2025 and enterprise value at $1.45bn (March 2026); Beckham told Forbes revenue reached $250m. MLS clubs publish no accounts, so wages, pre-tax result and net debt are blank. The Mas brothers' stake is Forbes' 'at least 70%' (recorded as 70, a floor); Ares holds preferred equity with no stated percentage; Messi has an option to take a small stake (Forbes). Jorge Mas was styled CEO and Managing Owner in 2021; 2026 club releases call him Managing Owner. Honours also include the 2023 Leagues Cup, 2024 Supporters' Shield and 2026 Campeones Cup (club history page). The ticket terms list the team entities: Inter Miami CF, LLC, Inter Miami FTL Stadium, LLC, Inter Miami Training Center, LLC, Inter Miami Stadium, LLC, Miami Freedom Park, LLC, Miami Beckham United, LLC and Fort Lauderdale USL, LLC. City changed from Fort Lauderdale to Miami: the first team moved to Nu Stadium in April 2026, while the Florida Blue Training Center and Inter Miami CF Stadium remain in Fort Lauderdale. Attendance and social follower counts were not found on a citable current page.

owners.name: Ares Management (funds managed by its Credit Group)

ownership_summary: Controlled by brothers Jorge Mas (managing owner) and Jose Mas, who own at least 70%, with David Beckham holding 26% (Forbes, May 2026). Beckham exercised his $25m MLS expansion option in 2014; the club launched in January 2018. In September 2021 the Mas brothers and Beckham bought out co-founders Marcelo Claure and Masayoshi Son's 48%, and Ares Management's Credit Group funds took $150m of preferred equity, adding $75m in August 2023. The same partners own the Miami Freedom Park venture that built Nu Stadium.
